established_facts: Accepted context is two-adult household, one decision maker, individually counted children, distinct first-child cost, and reference CEB 2.1; explicit child-age state expansion is ruled out by task.
Source stationary potential maturation-entry counter and dated birth queue use different clocks and conversion/unit conventions.
Source advancement applies survival before survivor maturation; terminal households and attached dependent counts exit.
Existing historical checkpoint explicitly records birth support through parent node 42, mortality beginning at 66, and dependent-loss flow. Its quantitative receipt is historical, not latest.
Existing newer frozen-parameter receipt confirms age survival but does not establish every setting needed for an accounting change.

derived_conclusions_not_empirical_estima: With literal two-adult households and no residual resident pool, common dependency exits conserve person counts only at c=1/2 after explicit migration/death flows; c=1/2.1 leaves 1/21 of retained departing persons unassigned.
Reference CEB 2.1 does not prove closed stationary replacement. Under internally consistent literal units and no reproductive mortality, c=1/2 implies 1.05 descendant couples per reference entrant.
Finite parent-age/n/m states cannot determine exact chronological offspring age for all fertility histories. A and C necessarily approximate age if all entrants start at model age 18.
A corrects disappearance without requiring an orphan-care model under verified late-mortality support, but assumes offspring survival while dependent and resets the economic lifecycle.
B can close a separate aggregate demographic stock only by ceasing to interpret m as literal household membership; cost/housing and transfer meaning must then be reconsidered.
A cap changes mean dependence and its response to birth timing. All-birth weights, first-draw timing, newborn exemption and fixed counterfactual hazard must be explicit.
A top-bin scalar pool cannot enforce parent-age-dependent release without additional parent-age information; a person ledger alone does not supply missing resource demands.

At fixed units and c, A adds cR to departure-only stationary renewal; without dependent death F=B. Its first entry response can occur after one four-year step, whereas the four-slot queue has a twenty-year effect lag. No equilibrium magnitude or sign is inferred.
